usage.notes: CellML is an interchange/encoding standard, not a network service. Panacea may ingest locally supplied or separately acquired CellML models and normalize them for simulation. Do not bundle a large model repository into the primary client; acquire models through explicit source adapters and cache only validated/versioned models needed by a feature.

license.scope: The official CellML terms allow individuals to freely use, publish and redistribute the CellML format/documentation; write and sell applications that create, load or write CellML-valid XML files; distribute or sell their own CellML-valid XML files; and transmit verbatim copies of the CellML format/documentation. Applications and files using the standard should reference the CellML specifications. These terms cover the CellML format/specification, not the copyright or license of every model encoded in CellML.
license.notes: Every imported model still needs its own model-level license/citation manifest. Do not infer that a .cellml file is commercially reusable merely because the CellML standard itself permits commercial implementations.

validation.notes: CellML 2.0 defines a valid model encoding, not whether a biological model is scientifically correct, calibrated for a population, validated against experiments, suitable for a patient or approved for clinical decisions. Syntax validity, numerical reproducibility and biological/clinical validity are separate gates.

provenance.authority: CellML Working Group / Auckland Bioengineering Institute / IUPS Physiome Project
provenance.notes: Record CellML specification version, model source/exposure, model authors, original publication/citation, model revision/commit or exposure identifier, acquisition timestamp and model license. Preserve component/variable names, units and semantic identifiers needed to audit transformations.

adapter.notes: Planned flow: provenance-cleared CellML model -> standards-compliant parser/validator -> normalized equations, variables, units, components and metadata -> PanaceaPhysiologyModelDefinition -> explicit simulation engine -> time-series outputs -> visualization. Persist solver name/version, parameters, initial conditions, time span, tolerances and output units with every simulation result. Never label interpolation or a hand-authored animation as model output.

trust.notes: High-authority modelling standard with strong reproducibility value. Evidence quality is intentionally low because a file format/specification is not biological evidence; each encoded model requires separate scientific validation.
